title: The three debt risks, plus a quiet fourth
objectives: Name interest-rate, credit, liquidity and reinvestment risk, and how each shows up.
Say how to reduce each risk.
body_md:
Debt is not risk-free; it carries different risks. Interest-rate risk: bond prices fall when rates rise, showing up as a gradual NAV fall — reduce it by matching fund duration to the goal date. Credit (default) risk: the borrower delays or fails to pay, or is downgraded, showing up as a sudden NAV drop — reduce it with high ratings and no yield chasing. Liquidity risk: bonds can't be sold quickly at a fair price, showing up as redemption delays — prefer liquid categories and large, diversified funds. Reinvestment risk, a fourth quieter one: maturing money must be reinvested at lower rates, so income falls over time.

| Risk | What it means | How it shows up | How to reduce it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Interest-rate risk | Bond prices fall when rates rise | Gradual NAV fall over weeks or months | Match fund duration to the goal date; shorter duration for near goals |
| Credit (default) risk | The borrower delays or fails to pay, or is downgraded | Sudden NAV drop, sometimes in a day | Stick to high ratings (AAA, sovereign); avoid chasing yield |
| Liquidity risk | Bonds can't be sold quickly at a fair price | Redemption delays, wide price gaps | Prefer liquid categories and large, diversified funds |
| Reinvestment risk (a fourth, quieter one) | Maturing money must be reinvested at lower rates | Income falls over time | Lock in longer maturities when rates are high, within the goal's horizon |

> **Investor takeaway:** Duration should match the goal date; credit quality should match how essential the money is.
example: A downgrade can cut NAV in a day (credit risk); a rate rise causes a gradual NAV dip (interest-rate risk) — different risks, different responses.
say: Debt has interest-rate, credit and liquidity risk; only the mix differs from equity.
Match duration to the goal; don't chase yield.
never: A sudden NAV drop is always interest-rate risk.
